traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 338 Boraginaceae (order Boraginales): herbs, often rough with stiff hairs; leaves alternate, very rarely opposite, simple; no stipules; flowers often in coiled (scorpioid) cymes, regular or rarely oblique; corolla united; stamens as many as its lobes; ovary superior, of two carpels, often deeply 4-lobed with the style from between the lobes; fruit of 4 nutlets, read here as a schizocarp. The family as Library 1.0 names it (WCVP) also holds Hutchinson's woody family 242 Ehretiaceae (Cordia, Ehretia, with drupes) and the waterleaf family (Hydrophyllum, Phacelia, with capsules): so woody, the drupe and the capsule are stated as sometimes (inferred, not traced).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Boraginaceae with Ehretiaceae, Hoplestigmataceae, Hydrophyllaceae, Lennoaceae, Wellstediaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.
